cautions: The confidence interval is wide compared with the trend, so the size of the change is uncertain.
ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in Western Europe changed by +0.048 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.016 to +0.079), which is statistically significant (p = 0.0039). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.118 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in Western Europe shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.12): the estimate is −0.0046 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.0106 to +0.0012). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in Western Europe shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.70): the estimate is +0.03 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.11 to +0.16). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
